home.description: Custom clothing for brands, businesses and teams. Our factory develops patterns and samples from your brief, from washed tees to tailored suits and technical outerwear.
home.eyebrow: Our garment factory in Yongqing, China
home.intro: Send a sketch, photo or sample. We develop the pattern, source the fabric and make your garments, from washed T-shirts and tailored suits to staff uniforms and technical outerwear.

faqs.q: Can we start with a reference image and no technical specification?
faqs.a: Yes. Send a photo, sketch or AI concept and tell us who will wear the clothing and how it will be used. We help work out the fabric, fit and construction, then develop a sample you can check. You do not need a finished tech pack to begin.

faqs.q: Can suits, polos, workwear and caps share the same brand identity?
faqs.a: Yes. Your reception, service and operations teams can wear different garments while sharing one brand identity. We use your colour references and artwork across the range, choosing suitable embroidery, printing or labels for each fabric. Samples let you check the items together before production.

faqs.q: How do semi-custom and fully custom orders differ in cost, minimums and timing?
faqs.a: If an existing garment already suits your team, start with logo, label or selected detail changes. Choose full development when you need a different fabric, fit, pocket layout or construction. Price depends on the development work, garment quantity and materials. Minimums and timing depend on the chosen style and changes.

faqs.q: Can you provide fabric reports or arrange finished-garment testing?
faqs.a: We can provide relevant fabric reports and arrange finished-garment testing. Include any required standard or performance requirement in your brief so the quote can account for it. Testing of custom finished garments carries an additional fee. Fabric reports cover the material; they do not certify the finished garment.

faqs.q: When does sampling start, and can you work to our event date?
faqs.a: Clothing samples take 7–12 days after order confirmation and sample payment. Tell us the date the garments need to arrive and the delivery destination, rather than only the event date. We plan backwards through shipping, production and sample approval. Production time depends on the products, materials, quantities and customisation.

faqs.q: Can we order one product category or a coordinated range?
faqs.a: Both are welcome. Send one list covering the clothing, caps, footwear, towels or PPE your team needs, with quantities for each item. LF brings the requirements together and coordinates the relevant suppliers, so your purchasing team has one point of contact. Options, minimums and schedules can vary by item.

faqs.q: Do you manufacture clothing in your own factory?
faqs.a: We manufacture garments in our own factory. LF handles specifications, materials, patterns, samples, production, quality checks and packing. Your team works directly with us from the initial brief to shipment.

faqs.q: How are PPE and construction safety helmets reviewed?
faqs.a: Tell us the product, intended use, destination and required standard. We check the supporting documents and whether the proposed colour, logo or other changes are suitable. PPE and helmet requirements are assessed for each product; clothing or fabric certificates do not automatically cover them.

customization.h1: From your reference image to your team’s clothing.
customization.intro: You do not need a finished technical specification to begin. Bring an image, an existing garment or an idea for your team. LF helps turn it into wearable clothing, from fabric and fit to pockets, lining and branding, with samples to check before production.
groupTitles: Patterns, fit, pockets and garment construction
Samples, feasibility review and specification approval

faqs.q: Can we develop uniforms from reference photos without a tech pack?
faqs.a: Yes. Photos, sketches and AI concept images can all start a project. Tell us the staff roles, working conditions and details that matter most. We work out how the concept can be made and prepare a physical sample for you to assess.

faqs.q: What if we do not know which fabric or processes to choose?
faqs.a: We first clarify how the garment will be used and any requirements for water resistance, breathability, texture and colour. We then select a suitable fabric and propose the matching construction, decoration and finishing methods. We send you the fabric choice and process proposal for confirmation before sampling.

faqs.q: Should we choose semi-custom or full garment development?
faqs.a: If your current uniform works well, start with branding or selected detail changes. For a different fabric, fit or construction, discuss full development. Send the reference and mark what you want to keep or change; we can explain which route fits the brief and how the changes affect price, quantity and timing.

faqs.q: What are your minimum order quantities?
faqs.a: The usual MOQ for regular clothing is 50 garments per style/colour. For specialist, complex garments such as flight suits and racing suits, quantities as low as 10 may be possible after review of the design, materials and production requirements. The lower minimum is limited to suitable specialist projects; it does not apply to ordinary event clothing.

faqs.q: Can different staff roles have different garments with coordinated branding?
faqs.a: Yes. Suits for reception, polos for service staff and workwear for operations can share colours and branding while keeping the fit and details each role needs. Check the fabric and logo samples together to see how the range works as a whole.

faqs.q: Can products other than clothing be customised?
faqs.a: Yes. Include caps, footwear, towels or other related items in the same brief. Available materials, colours, dimensions and branding vary by product. For PPE and safety helmets, include the required standard and destination so we can check suitable products and permitted changes.

faqs.q: What information helps you quote our uniforms or event clothing?
faqs.a: Start with your item list, estimated quantities, reference images, destination and required arrival date. Add sizes, artwork and any testing requirements if you have them. If some details are still undecided, tell us your priorities and we will help you narrow the options. Sample fees are quoted for the project. For orders of 200 pieces or more of the same style, the sample fee can be credited against the bulk order payment.

faqs.q: Can you arrange fabric and finished-garment test reports?
faqs.a: Yes. We can arrange fabric and finished-garment testing and provide the resulting reports. Tell us the properties or standards you need to assess. Custom finished-garment tests carry an additional fee, with scope and cost discussed before testing. The report applies to the tested material or garment, rather than certifying every product in the range.

faqs.q: How do you keep a reference for repeat orders?
faqs.a: We retain one garment from each bulk order as a physical reference. It helps us align fit, construction and branding when you order again. Share the previous order reference and any required changes. Materials and trims are checked for availability before the repeat order is arranged.

samplingFaqs.q: How much does a clothing sample cost?
samplingFaqs.a: We quote the sample fee after reviewing your requirements. It is usually around twice the bulk unit price. The exact amount is confirmed in your quotation.

samplingFaqs.q: Can the sample fee be credited against a bulk order?
samplingFaqs.a: For orders of 200 pieces or more of the same style, the sample fee can be credited against the bulk order payment.

samplingFaqs.q: Does the sample fee include adjustments?
samplingFaqs.a: The sample fee includes adjustments within a reasonable scope. We work through your feedback until the sample achieves the agreed result. Bulk production follows the approved sample and confirmed specifications.

samplingFaqs.q: How are samples shipped, and is shipping included?
samplingFaqs.a: Sample shipping is charged separately. Samples are usually sent by express courier on DDP terms.

productionFaqs.q: How long does bulk production take, and what deposit is required?
productionFaqs.a: For regular bulk orders of up to 500 pieces, production usually takes 2–3 weeks from receipt of the 30% deposit. Shipping time is additional.

productionFaqs.q: When is the balance due, and can we inspect the order?
productionFaqs.a: We require a 30% deposit, with the remaining 70% balance paid in full before shipment. Video inspection and in-person inspection are available before dispatch.

productionFaqs.q: How do you check and pack the order before dispatch?
productionFaqs.a: We record quality inspection and packing videos before shipment. Garments with obvious quality or appearance issues identified during inspection are remade before packing and are not dispatched with those issues.

productionFaqs.q: How are defects in a delivered bulk order handled?
productionFaqs.a: If defects are found after delivery, we review the issues against the approved sample and specifications. Compensation is agreed case by case, taking the defect rate and other relevant factors into account.
